stop_condition: every acceptance criterion in the task description is traced to an executed assertion; the R1-F1 write-confirmation gate is proven non-vacuous with a restore control and a discriminator; design_conflict_write_unconfirmed and design_conflict_confirm_unreadable are proven observably distinct and neither asserts more than it knows; the confirmation gate's stated uniqueness basis is verified rather than assumed; and no critical/high finding remains in the design-conflict writer, reader, or the newly-wired producer prose

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:10915-10921 (the confirmation gate's justification comment) and :10923 (the raw-text match it justifies)
findings.evidence: MEASURED, forced deterministically rather than raced, and reproduced TWICE in two independently-written fixtures. Instrument: a `date` shim returning a fixed 2026-09-09T09:09:09Z for the exact format string cmd_design_conflict uses, so two calls compute an IDENTICAL to-the-second ts without racing a 1-second window; everything else real bd. Probe 1 A-series: call 1 (frozen clock, healthy store) recorded, and exactly ONE matching record existed on the design task (A.3). Call 2 -- SAME frozen clock, SAME --unit U1, SAME statement, write killed by a shim failing both `bd comments add` and `bd comment add` -- returned rc=0 {"ok":true,"subcommand":"design-conflict","status":"recorded",...} while the record count stayed at exactly ONE (A.4), i.e. call 2's own write never landed and it matched call 1's byte-identical record. Probe 2 D1.1/D1.2 re-confirmed independently. SO THE COMMENT'S CLAIM IS FALSE AS WRITTEN: 'comment_text is unique per call -- it embeds the to-the-second timestamp and the free-text statement -- so an exact match cannot mean "some OTHER conflict record happens to be present"'. An exact match CAN mean exactly that. Same claim restated in the task notes and in the specialist's completion contract `decisions`.
findings.description: NOT BLOCKING, and the reason is measured rather than argued -- five separate legs. (1) THE GATE'S ACTUAL GUARANTEE HOLDS: in the collision state design-gate-precheck refuses rc=4 error_key=design_conflict_open (probe D2.1/D2.2) and cmd_approve ITSELF refuses design_conflict_open (probe D3.1, driven with --no-design/--no-review/--no-completion/--no-impact-report so the design-conflict refusal is what fires). So this is categorically NOT the R1-F1 defect family: R1-F1 was a FAIL-OPEN that could ship a design nobody re-reviewed; this cannot ship anything. (2) A BYTE-IDENTICAL MATCH IS NECESSARILY AN OPEN RECORD, structurally, not by luck: identical text implies identical unit_hash, and unit_hash is re-pinned to the disputed unit's CURRENT content on every call, so current_hash == row_hash at :11219 and the record stays OPEN. A cleared record therefore cannot masquerade as the caller's fresh filing. (3) THE RECORD IS FUNGIBLE BY GRAMMAR: DESIGN-CONFLICT carries no filed_by/from_task field at all (the residual I recorded as R1-F4), so two records with identical bytes are indistinguishable by design -- there is no 'wrong record' to confirm when nothing distinguishes them, and the reader dedups repeats anyway (the `seen` guard at :11220-11223). (4) THE RETRY ROUTE POSITED IN THE BRIEF DOES NOT REACH IT: write_unconfirmed fires only when the record is genuinely absent, so on a retry-after-refusal no identical prior record exists to match. The one retry route in is a retry after confirm_unreadable (write landed, could not be verified) -- and there the operator's belief 'the conflict is filed' is TRUE. (5) THE LOST WRITE IS NOT SILENTLY SWALLOWED: sync-errors.log records it (probe D1.3, measured line `bd comments add failed for <design-task> (msg=DESIGN-CONFLICT U1 design_hash=...)`), which SessionStart surfaces. So the residual is a false claim about WHICH invocation wrote a fungible record, not a gating error. What makes it a finding rather than nothing is that the false claim is LOAD-BEARING PROSE: it is the stated reason a raw-text match is 'strictly stronger' than re-parsing the grammar, and a future editor relying on it could drop the statement from the match, or reuse the 'unique per call' reasoning for a record type where duplicates ARE semantically distinct. SUGGESTED FIX, either half suffices: (a) correct the comment to state the basis that is actually true and provable -- fungibility plus necessarily-open -- or (b) make the confirmation per-invocation by capturing the subject's comment set (or the ids) BEFORE add_comment and requiring a NEW matching entry afterwards.

findings.evidence: print_envelope_checked's ENVELOPE-SHAPE-GATE registers a shape for design-unit-show and design-status only; every other subcommand falls to `*) shape_prog='false'`, which always fails and prints envelope_construction_failed. So routing design-conflict through that helper WITHOUT also registering a shape would have hard-failed the success path -- the implementer's choice of a raw `printf` plus the `envelope=$(jq -nc ...) || rc=$?` discipline (correctly citing the xsu1 H2-F4 inlined-substitution lesson) was the right minimal call for a LOW envelope-only change, and its fallback to emit_json 1 (verified: emit_json's first arg 1 means ok:true, :2613-2625) is safe.
findings.description: Residual only, recorded so it does not drift. R1-F4's whole purpose was to make the resolved subject MACHINE-READABLE as design_task rather than findable only inside free-text observations. The moment something actually machine-reads it, this envelope has no shape validation while the precedent it cites (design-unit-show) does -- the exact asymmetry the ENVELOPE-SHAPE-GATE exists to prevent for accessors. Cheap follow-up: register a design-conflict shape in that case block when a consumer appears. Verified there is no such consumer today.

findings.location: method finding -- not a defect in this change set; concerns how live-store residue is swept (brief item 4)
findings.evidence: MEASURED in an isolated fixture: task created with updated_at=2026-09-09T10:41:56Z and comment_count=0; after `bd comments add`, comment_count went 0 -> 1 while updated_at stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL at 2026-09-09T10:41:56Z. Corroborated on the live task under review: claude-workflow-plugin-268l still reports updated_at=2026-09-09T07:47:17Z with comment_count=8 after my own 07:53:06 `enter`. Schema check also confirms the field is created_at/updated_at, never `.created`.
findings.description: Any sweep for probe-authored records that scopes by updated_at is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to a comment written onto a legitimate task -- which is precisely the residue class item 4 asked me to hunt, and precisely what a whole-task delete would not catch. Both the coordinator's sweep and my own first pass used that blind instrument and would have reported clean. Redone against the authoritative instrument (the dolt `comments` table, all 12365 rows): every one of the 22 comments created on 2026-09-09 belongs to a legitimate task and a legitimate record type, and a store-wide text sweep for fixture-shaped ids returns only prose mentions inside real QA notes. Store genuinely clean; nothing to add to .beads/quarantine.tsv.

findings.evidence: MEASURED (probe 3, isolated fixture, hypothesised from reading design_comments_json at :1827-1852 and then tested rather than asserted). Bound a unit task to a design task, confirmed filing works, then DELETED the design task while leaving its docs/specs/<id>.md on disk -- so the artifact check at :10763 still passes, the DESIGN-UNIT binding still resolves (design-unit-show bound:true), and the write is then attempted against a task that no longer exists. Result: rc=5 error_key=design_conflict_confirm_unreadable, message 'the write was submitted but the confirmation re-read of <design-task>'s own comment stream failed right now (bd unreachable, the stream not retrievable, or unparseable) -- whether the conflict record landed is unknown, and no claim is made about it either way. Once bd is reachable, verify with: qa-gate.sh design-gate-precheck <tid> ...'.
findings.description: The DISPOSITION is right and this is NOT the failure item 2 was worried about: it is fail-CLOSED (exit 5, nothing claimed recorded) and it does NOT overclaim -- it says the outcome is unknown rather than asserting the record is absent, which is the distinction that matters. The imprecision is in the CAUSE LIST and the REMEDIATION: the real cause here is that $subject no longer exists (so the write definitively did NOT land), yet the enumerated causes are all connectivity/parse faults and the remedy is 'Once bd is reachable', which sends the operator to look at bd health rather than at a dangling DESIGN-UNIT binding. 'Unknown' is conservative in the SAFE direction, so severity is low. Root cause is upstream and pre-existing, not introduced here: design_comments_json returns the same rc 3 for 'no such task' as for 'unreadable', which is itself the correct conservative choice. Cheap fix if wanted: name the dangling-binding possibility in the cause list, since resolve_design_conflict_subject already knows subject_bound=true. Worth recording because a unit task bound to a deleted design task is now permanently un-approvable (design-gate-precheck refuses via the same rc-3 propagation) with an error that points away from the actual cause.
